svg.text: Anatomy of a narrative: context in layers, then depth, then the record

g.text: # The question, exactly as asked
one question per narrative; the file name is its slug
1 · Abstract
the problem, the answer, 3–5 key takeaways · ≤150 words
2 · Terminology
the few terms the whole narrative leans on, every abbreviation
3 … · The template's sections
the first one orients: what, where and when, who, why
then the answer, on one running example worked with numbers;
every claim cited to a section, [→] ours, [?] a gap;
diagrams and figures with numbered captions; links to related narratives
Appendix · SMEs · References · Metadata

svg.text: glossary and secondary detail; who to ask; sources read and citations;
version, model, history and the reading plan, kept by finish-narrative

g.text: For a reader deciding whether to read on,
and for an agent answering a query:
most questions stop at the Abstract
For a reader learning it:
the template decides the shape (concept, technical,
survey, comparison, case study), its aim decides
the balance, and lint grades the aim
For a reviewer checking it:
what was read, in what order, by which model;
each citation opens the exact source section
